correctness.rationale: For a transitive subtournament of the cyclic tournament, its source forces every vertex into one cyclic block, proving \(\operatorname{dFl}(R_n)=\mathcal N(n,m)\). Reversing \(0\to1\) preserves all old faces, makes only \(\{0,1,m+1\}\) newly transitive, and no fourth vertex can join it because an unchanged directed 3-cycle results on either side. The three corresponding circular arcs form a good subcover of \(S^1\) with nerve equal to that triangle boundary, so by naturality of the nerve theorem its inclusion in \(\mathcal N(n,m)\) is a homotopy equivalence. The simplicial pushout obtained by filling it is therefore contractible. The bundled finite reconstruction through \(n=17\) independently checks the exact face change and acyclicity over \(\mathbb F_2\).

value.rationale: The cyclic tournament is the canonical all-order regular locally transitive model whose directed flag complex carries the exceptional circle homotopy. Showing that one natural adjacent outcome flip adds exactly one triangle and kills that homotopy in every odd order is a structural stability boundary, not a parameter substitution or isolated table lookup. The exact “one simplex fills the generator” mechanism is reusable when studying sensitivity of tournament topology to local edge perturbations.
